after_notes: Phase 05 route shell and firmware build cover API/log/command routes. Phase 10 manifest/tooling evidence in `docs/parity/evidence/phase-10-route-manifest-and-api-compare-unification.md` proves firmware reporting and API compare consume `phase07_routes()` for OTA, OTAWWW, recovery, and static route policy. Phase 17 live HTTP/static/API evidence in `docs/parity/evidence/phase-17-live-http-api-and-static-evidence/http-static-api.md` and `summary.md` records a sanitized `target-lock.json`, `network_scan: disabled`, and passed route artifacts for `/`, `/assets/app.css.gz`, missing static redirect, `/recovery`, `/api/system/info`, unknown `/api/*`, `/api/ws`, `/api/ws/live`, `POST /api/system/OTA`, and `POST /api/system/OTAWWW`. WebSocket no-upgrade checks are route-coexistence only, and OTA route checks are route-presence only. Later evidence, outside the artifacts above, adds the access gate, `is_network_allowed` in the same upstream file. `firmware/bitaxe/src/http_api/access.rs` now reads the peer of the `PF_INET6` server socket as `sockaddr_in6`, and `crates/bitaxe-api/src/route_shell.rs` denies a peer that is unreadable, zero or not IPv4-mapped, which fixes a read that left the gate checking only the Origin. `just access-gate-check` on production Gamma 601 `6269d90c` and Ultra 205 `0c0698db` returned 200 with no Origin, 200 with a private Origin and 401 with a public Origin; see `docs/parity/evidence/20261030-access-gate-peer-address.md`. A public peer being denied is shown by unit tests only, and a real IPv6 peer, the WebSocket routes, and settings and OTA routes through this gate are not shown on hardware. Known differences from upstream: a real IPv6 peer is always denied where upstream classifies its last four bytes; an Origin with a port, `https://` or no scheme is accepted where upstream denies it; `/recovery` is not gated where upstream gates it. The earlier limits still apply.
